findings.title: Ledger-failure test omits the reset_ai_credits assertion required by SPEC 9.1
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC.md 9.1: the webhook spec must verify existing branch behavior byte-identical around the insertion — 'the org update, payment-method call, reset_ai_credits still happen; a ledger failure does not break them'. 'Them' enumerates all three behaviors.
findings.evidence: spec/jobs/stripe_webhook_handler_subscription_events_spec.rb:131-140 (committed at 89286fba8): the example 'does not break the existing branch behavior when the ledger write raises' stubs CreateSubscriptionEvent.call to raise StandardError and asserts stripe_current_period_end_at persisted (line 138) and stripe_update_default_payment_method received (line 139), but never stubs/asserts organization_ai_credit_balance.reset_ai_credits. The success-path example at lines 120-129 asserts all three; the failure-path example covers only two of the three enumerated behaviors. reset_ai_credits is the statement immediately preceding the insertion point (app/jobs/stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb:311 in the committed file), making it the most adjacent behavior to the new code and the one most worth asserting under ledger failure.
findings.recommendation: In the 'does not break the existing branch behavior when the ledger write raises' example, add `organization_ai_credit_balance = organization.organization_ai_credit_balance` + `allow(organization_ai_credit_balance).to receive(:reset_ai_credits)` before performing, and `expect(organization_ai_credit_balance).to have_received(:reset_ai_credits)` after, mirroring lines 121-128.

verified: D11 delicacy: git diff a0d59115d..89286fba8 on app/jobs/stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb is 34 insertions, 0 deletions, exactly two purely-additive hunks matching the two sanctioned insertion points; no branch reordering, no attribute-access changes, no cleanup anywhere in the file

Placement: insertion 1 is appended at the END of the invoice.paid main-plan else-branch body, immediately after organization.organization_ai_credit_balance&.reset_ai_credits and before the branch-closing end; every pre-existing statement executes before the new block; no other line in the branch changed

Isolation: the block carries its OWN begin/rescue StandardError that logs with context (Rails.logger.error with org/invoice/subscription/msg, plus ap e, matching the branch's existing tier style); Stripe::StripeError and the ActiveRecord errors are StandardError descendants, so a ledger failure can never reach the branch's three pre-existing rescue tiers or alter completed behavior

Predicate exact per SPEC 4: object.amount_paid.to_i > 0 cash gate; stripe_subscription.trial_end.present? selects 'trial_converted_to_paid', absent selects 'converted_to_paid'; uses the stripe_subscription local the branch ALREADY assigns from Stripe::Subscription.retrieve(object.subscription) — not the event payload snapshot, no status field, no billing_reason; evaluated after the raise CustomStripeSubscriptionMissingError guard

Writer call exact per SPEC 5.2: CreateSubscriptionEvent.call(organization: organization, event_type: <per predicate>, to_plan: organization.plan, stripe_subscription_id: object.subscription, amount: object.amount_paid); from_plan omitted so it persists nil (from_plan asserted nil in both positive-cell tests)

Duplicate handling: CreateSubscriptionEvent check-first conversion_duplicate_exists? queries SubscriptionEvent::CONVERSION_EVENT_TYPES (= converted_to_paid + trial_converted_to_paid, subscription_event.rb) by stripe_subscription_id alone; context.fail! is caught by the Interactor gem's .call so the webhook caller sees no raise; raced ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique rescued to the same graceful fail. Cross-type guard non-vacuously tested in spec/interactors/create_subscription_event_spec.rb:17-58 (different event_type defeats the 5-minute same-params dedupe, so those examples isolate the uniqueness guard)

D10 style: event-type selection is a full if/else expression assigned to subscription_event_type; no .presence anywhere in the insertion; no early returns added; the cash gate is an if-block (no bail-out semantics misused)

House-safe attribute access: only plain field reads (object.amount_paid, object.subscription, stripe_subscription.trial_end) consistent with the branch's pre-existing forms (object.subscription, stripe_subscription.current_period_end); no metadata access added

Tests exist at the SPEC 9.1 path spec/jobs/stripe_webhook_handler_subscription_events_spec.rb; full predicate matrix (amount_paid 0/4900 x trial_end present/nil) stubbing Stripe::Subscription.retrieve; positive cells assert count +1, event_type, amount, stripe_subscription_id, to_plan, from_plan nil — non-vacuous (fail if the insertion were deleted)

Duplicate delivery test asserts exactly one row across two identical perform_now calls and no raise; non-vacuous (fails if the feature were deleted). Note: both deliveries fall inside the 5-minute dedupe window, so this example alone does not isolate the conversion-uniqueness guard from the pre-existing dedupe — the guard is isolated by the interactor spec's cross-type examples (different event_type), so the required behavior chain is covered

Existing-behavior test (success path) asserts all three behaviors: stripe_current_period_end_at persisted to the stubbed subscription's current_period_end, stripe_update_default_payment_method received, reset_ai_credits received

Test scaffolding genuinely reaches the main-plan branch: create_credit_test_organization (spec/support/ai_credits_test_helpers.rb:21-73) sets stripe_customer_id/stripe_subscription_id, and the stubbed lookup key 'plan_ats_tier_starter_v2_monthly' is not in Variables::AI_CREDIT_ALLOCATIONS (config/initializers/01_variables.rb:132-147), so ai_credit_subscription_plan_lookup_key? is false and the else branch executes; queue adapter :test around-block present per pipeline rule 31
SPEC 11.6 rollout misclassification is disclosed-open — implementation as specced, not treated as a finding
